blocks.text: FloppyData in 2026: what you get

FloppyData sells proxies the way prepaid phone plans sell minutes: one flat $1/GB balance that works across residential, mobile and datacenter pools. Static residential IPs start at $1.79 each in monthly bundles (20 for $49) with unlimited bandwidth. It is one of the cheapest ways into residential traffic, but it is a newer brand with less independent benchmarking than the established names.

Strengths: Flat $1/GB on any volume; One balance across residential, mobile and datacenter; Cheap static residential bundles with unlimited bandwidth; Free cloud anti-detect browser. Weak spots: Newer brand with limited independent testing; Pool-size claims disputed by some reviewers; Mixed customer-support reviews.
IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal built its reputation on flexible, non-expiring residential bandwidth and straightforward pricing. The pool is smaller than the enterprise networks at 32M+ advertised IPs, but it covers 195 countries, supports SOCKS5, and offers some of the longest sticky sessions available (up to seven days). Its headline $1.75/GB rate only applies at 10 TB; most buyers will pay between $5 and $7 per GB on small orders.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Pricing: FloppyData vs IPRoyal

FloppyData charges a flat $1/GB for rotating traffic, and the same balance works for residential, mobile and datacenter IPs. Static residential proxies are sold in monthly bundles from $1.79 per IP (20 IPs for $49), and static datacenter IPs from $0.79 per IP.

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

At 10 GB a month, FloppyData is the cheaper option at about $10 against $52.50 for IPRoyal, roughly 81% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; FloppyData comes to about $100. Look past the per-GB figure too. IPRoyal lets unused traffic carry forward, while FloppyData's allowance does not (check current terms). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

FloppyData does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. FloppyData lists '65M+ claimed (disputed)' and IPRoyal lists '32M+'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, FloppyData lists 148 (residential) countries and IPRoyal lists 195. On targeting, FloppyData offers country and city, while IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, FloppyData offers rotating or sticky sessions, and IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. How FloppyData compares: cheap, but with limited independent benchmarking.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. FloppyData: workable for light tasks. IPRoyal: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. How FloppyData compares: cheap static residential IPs and a free anti-detect browser.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. The limitation on the FloppyData side: city targeting at a flat rate.

Ad verification and geo-testing: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts. The limitation on the FloppyData side: limited targeting depth and published data.
Tight budgets: FloppyData. FloppyData has the edge here. Why: a flat $1/GB on any volume. How IPRoyal compares: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. FloppyData: No free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Verification and payment rules differ too. FloppyData: Light. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test FloppyData and IPRoyal before you commit
The quickest way to choose between FloppyData and IPRoyal is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (FloppyData: no free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations; IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, FloppyData comes out ahead in 1, IPRoyal in 4, and 1 is a tie. That makes IPRoyal the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: FloppyData is strongest for small budgets and experiments, while IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
